back: Define what the engine must do before designing how it does it. Torque, RPM range, thermal limits.
Wankel cycle: intake→compression→ignition→exhaust. Rotor has 3 faces, each fires once per revolution.
Apex seals: carbon-aluminum or ceramic. Housing: Nikasil-coated aluminum. Thermal expansion must match.
Every dimension has a tolerance. The stack of tolerances determines whether parts fit at temperature.
First physical article. Differences from CAD are inevitable — CMM measures exactly how much.
Assembly order matters. Apex seals inserted last. Housing bolts torqued in spiral pattern from center.
First 10 hours: vary RPM, no full load. Seals bed into housing. Compression rises then stabilizes.
validation: Compression stabilizes within 5% across all 3 chambers

back: Full-throttle sweep from idle to redline. Measures actual output against design predictions.
validation: Within 3% of design targets across RPM range

back: Extended run at peak torque RPM. Measures how the engine ages. Catches fatigue before production.
validation: No catastrophic failure, wear within spec

back: Design frozen. Manufacturing process documented. Quality gates defined at every station.
validation: First article inspection passed, PPAP approved
